requirements.name: go-module-decoder-command
requirements.text: Establish the standard-library-only Go module and decoder command.

requirements.name: stdin-tagged-json-contract
requirements.text: The program is a filter: read TOML from **stdin**, write tagged JSON to **stdout**, exit `0`.

requirements.name: parse-toml-strings
requirements.text:
- **Scalars** — booleans, integers (including `0x`, `0o`, `0b`, underscores), floats (including `inf`, `nan`, exponents), basic and literal strings, then
  multi-line strings with their line-ending backslash and trimming rules.

requirements.name: parse-lexical-scalars
requirements.text:
- **Scalars** — booleans, integers (including `0x`, `0o`, `0b`, underscores),
  floats (including `inf`, `nan`, exponents), basic and literal strings, then
  multi-line strings with their line-ending backslash and trimming rules.

requirements.name: parse-lexical-boundaries
requirements.text:
- **Scaffolding** — line handling, comments, whitespace, the stdin/stdout/exit
  contract, tagged JSON emission.

requirements.name: parse-key-semantics
requirements.text: - **Keys** — bare, quoted, and dotted keys; the redefinition rules.

requirements.name: parse-tables
requirements.text:
- **Tables** — `[table]`, `[a.b.c]` implicit creation, `[[array of tables]]`,
  and the rules governing which of these may follow which.

requirements.name: parse-arrays-inline-tables
requirements.text:
- **Inline tables and arrays** — including nesting and the TOML 1.0 restriction
  that inline tables are closed to later extension.

requirements.name: parse-datetimes
requirements.text: - **Datetimes** — offset, local datetime, local date, local time.

requirements.name: pass-complete-conformance-suite
requirements.text: - `sh sources/full_test.sh` runs cleanly with zero errors and exits zero.

requirements.name: pin-test-version
requirements.text: The version setup_harness.sh installs. run_conformance.sh refuses a different one, so a passing verdict names a specific exam rather than whichever harness was on PATH.

requirements.name: build-decoder
requirements.text: go build -o toml-decoder ./cmd/toml-decoder

requirements.name: run-conformance-suite
requirements.text: DECODER="$PWD/toml-decoder" exec sh sources/run_conformance.sh

requirements.name: run-toml-conformance
requirements.text: Run the upstream toml-test conformance suite against the built decoder.

requirements.name: standardize-harness-exit-status
requirements.text: Exit code follows the harness exit-status standard in prompts/UAT_SETUP_INSTRUCTIONS.md: 0 only when every test passes, 2 when this harness could not run at all, and any other nonzero when it ran and the decoder failed.

requirements.name: install-conformance-harness
requirements.text: One-time installation of the upstream toml-test conformance harness.

requirements.name: architecture-stage-gate
requirements.text:
test -f go.mod
    if grep -Eq '^[[:space:]]*require[[:space:](]' go.mod; then
      echo "go.mod declares a forbidden third-party dependency" >&2
      exit 1
    fi
    go build ./cmd/toml-decoder

requirements.name: decoder-stage-gate
requirements.text:
printf 'answer = 42\n' | ./toml-decoder >"$stage_dir/valid.json" 2>"$stage_dir/valid.err"
    test ! -s "$stage_dir/valid.err"
    python - "$stage_dir/valid.json" <<'PY'
import json
import sys

with open(sys.argv[1], encoding="utf-8") as stream:
    decoded = json.load(stream)
assert decoded == {"answer": {"type": "integer", "value": "42"}}
PY

    if printf 'answer = [\n' | ./toml-decoder >"$stage_dir/invalid.out" 2>"$stage_dir/invalid.err"; then
      echo "malformed TOML exited successfully" >&2
      exit 1
    fi
    test ! -s "$stage_dir/invalid.out"
    test -s "$stage_dir/invalid.err"

requirements.name: require-single-pattern-argument
requirements.text:
if [ $# -ne 1 ]; then
  echo "usage: stage_test.sh <toml-test -run pattern>" >&2
  exit 2
fi

requirements.name: set-test-version
requirements.text:
TOML_TEST_VERSION="${TOML_TEST_VERSION:-v2.2.0}"
export TOML_TEST_VERSION

requirements.name: build-decoder
requirements.text: go build -o toml-decoder ./cmd/toml-decoder

requirements.name: run-authoritative-test-slice
requirements.text: DECODER="$PWD/toml-decoder" exec sh sources/run_conformance.sh -run "$1"

requirements.name: preserve-test-verdict
requirements.text: Exit status is the verdict and the whole verdict. Do not filter, skip, or reinterpret.

requirements.name: document-lexical-rules
requirements.text:
* TOML is case-sensitive.
* A TOML file must be a valid UTF-8 encoded Unicode document.
* Whitespace means tab (0x09) or space (0x20).
* Newline means LF (0x0A) or CRLF (0x0D 0x0A).

A hash symbol marks the rest of the line as a comment, except when inside a
string.

requirements.name: key-definition-semantics
requirements.text: A key may be either bare, quoted, or dotted.

requirements.name: scalar-values
requirements.text:
Values must have one of the following types.

- [String](#string)
- [Integer](#integer)
- [Float](#float)
- [Boolean](#boolean)
- [Offset Date-Time](#offset-date-time)
- [Local Date-Time](#local-date-time)
- [Local Date](#local-date)
- [Local Time](#local-time)
- [Array](#array)
- [Inline Table](#inline-table)

requirements.name: string-values
requirements.text:
There are four ways to express strings: basic, multi-line basic, literal, and
multi-line literal. All strings must contain only valid UTF-8 characters.

requirements.name: datetime-values
requirements.text:
To unambiguously represent a specific instant in time, you may use an [RFC
3339](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc3339) formatted date-time with offset.

requirements.name: arrays-and-inline-tables
requirements.text:
Arrays are square brackets with values inside. Whitespace is ignored. Elements
are separated by commas.

Inline tables provide a more compact syntax for expressing tables.

requirements.name: tables-and-arrays-of-tables
requirements.text:
Tables (also known as hash tables or dictionaries) are collections of key/value
pairs. They are defined by headers, with square brackets on a line by
themselves.

The last syntax that has not yet been described allows writing arrays of tables.

requirements.name: toml-file-extension
requirements.text: TOML files should use the extension `.toml`.

requirements.name: toml-mime-type
requirements.text:
When transferring TOML files over the internet, the appropriate MIME type is
`application/toml`.
